topic: Node.js tracer heap leak and OOM crashes in a Next.js app, resolved by disabling the Undici integration
environment: Next.js 16 App Router, standalone output, cacheComponents enabled
symptom_pattern: With tracing enabled, V8 heap grows without bound (about 35-50 MiB/h). The pods eventually crash with 'Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit' at about 30h of uptime, and users see 502 bursts. The growth began after a tracer upgrade. Disabling the tracer entirely stopped the crashes immediately.
root_cause: Engineering traced the leak to the tracer's Undici integration. The customer's observation matched a known upstream issue where finished spans are retained because long-lived async resources capture the AsyncLocalStorage frame. Engineering merged a tracer-side fix and opened a fix against the Undici project as well. The thread does not give more detail on the mechanism.
resolution_path: The customer had set DD_TRACE_ENABLED=false as a stopgap, which stopped the OOM crashes but left the service without APM.
The TSE asked whether the issue started with the tracer upgrade, and the customer confirmed the regression window and that the crashes stopped when tracing was disabled.
The TSE escalated to Engineering with the regression window and the customer's offer to supply heap snapshots.
Engineering identified the Undici integration as the likely cause.
The TSE gave two workarounds: set DD_TRACE_UNDICI_ENABLED=false, or call tracer.use('undici', false).
The customer re-enabled tracing with the Undici integration disabled. They validated it in staging for 24 hours, then in production, where memory plateaued.
Engineering merged the tracer-side fix, due in the next tracer release.
Engineering confirmed the customer can re-enable the Undici integration after upgrading to that release.
info_needed: Whether the issue began with the tracer upgrade, and the tracer version before and after
Whether any other application changes happened around the time the issue started

qa_pairs.tse_question: Have you been experiencing this issue since upgrading the tracer from 5.87.0 to 5.113.0? If not, did anything change in the application around the time it started?
qa_pairs.customer_answer: Yes. Memory was stable on the older tracer version, climbed after the upgrade and led to OOM crashes. Setting DD_TRACE_ENABLED=false with no other changes stopped the crashes immediately, which isolated the tracer from the other dependency bumps.

customer_style.tone: polite, appreciative, and well prepared, having researched the upstream issue before opening the ticket

evidence: FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit

tse_approach.summary: The TSE took the customer's detailed report and escalated it to Engineering. They asked a targeted question about when the issue started, which narrowed the regression window. They then relayed Engineering's workaround and kept the customer updated until the fix was merged.
steps: Passed on Engineering's question about the tracer version change and when the issue began.
Confirmed the regression window with the customer and forwarded it to Engineering.
Relayed Engineering's root-cause finding and gave two ways to disable the Undici integration.
Updated the customer when the tracer-side fix was merged and a fix was opened in the Undici project.
Asked Engineering whether the integration could be re-enabled right after the tracer fix or only after the Undici fix.
Relayed Engineering's answer that the integration can be re-enabled after upgrading to the next tracer release.
key_questions: Have you been experiencing this issue since upgrading the tracer, and did anything else change in the application around that time?
Can the Undici integration be re-enabled right after the tracer fix, or only after the Undici-side fix is released? (asked of Engineering on the customer's behalf)
